findings.premise: assert.deepEqual, as imported from node:assert/strict in this file, is typed with the assertion signature 'asserts actual is T' (aliased to deepStrictEqual), which is the mechanism the design's stated root cause (TS narrows `replies`/`acks` after the call) depends on.
findings.evidence: The test file imports `assert from 'node:assert/strict'` (router-session.test.ts:13). @types/node/assert/strict.d.ts re-exports `deepStrictEqual as deepEqual` (line 86), and @types/node/assert.d.ts:588 declares `function deepStrictEqual<T>(actual: unknown, expected: T, message?): asserts actual is T;` — the plain (non-strict) `deepEqual` at assert.d.ts:468 has no such signature, confirming the narrowing is specific to the strict import this file uses, matching the design's claim. [files: src/daemon/threads/__tests__/router-session.test.ts, node_modules/@types/node/assert/strict.d.ts, node_modules/@types/node/assert.d.ts]

summary.prose: Makes src/daemon/threads/__tests__/router-session.test.ts type-check cleanly against its own types. Two assert.deepEqual calls were, by TypeScript's own narrowing rules for that assertion's type signature, silently narrowing two local arrays to types too narrow for the values pushed into them later in the same tests — invisible today because the project's own tsc --noEmit excludes test files. Casting the expected literal at each call site to the variable's actual declared type removes the narrowing with zero change to any test's runtime behavior.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

dataModelChanges.details: No type or shape of any production or test API changes. Two assert.deepEqual call sites gain a type cast on their expected argument (as (ReplyEnvelope | FrameEnvelope)[] for replies, as string[] for acks), and the file gains a type-only import of ReplyEnvelope/FrameEnvelope from channel.ts (already exported, already imported the same way by router.ts). No runtime value, assertion outcome, or test behavior changes. [[c1]]

edgeCases.input: A future assert.deepEqual(x, <literal>) call added to this file reintroduces the same narrowing pattern for a different variable.
edgeCases.expected: Out of scope for this Story (noted as a residual risk in the rejected alternatives) — not something this fix can structurally prevent, since the narrowing is inherent to assert.deepEqual's TypeScript signature, not to this file's current code.

invariantsToPreserve.text: Every test's runtime assertion outcome (what passes, what fails, and why) is unchanged — the Story's Fix intent requires 'every test asserts exactly what it asserts today'; confirmed by running all 21 tests in the file before and after the two casts with identical pass results.
Nothing outside src/daemon/threads/__tests__/router-session.test.ts changes — ReplyEnvelope/FrameEnvelope are consumed as already-exported read-only types from channel.ts, not modified.

migration.stateBefore: src/daemon/threads/__tests__/router-session.test.ts has 6 TS2345 errors when type-checked on its own (confirmed via a temporary including tsconfig), invisible to the project's own tsc --noEmit since tsconfig.json excludes test files. replies (unknown[], line 505) and acks (string[], line 543) each get narrowed by an assert.deepEqual call whose expected literal has a type too narrow for later pushes/includes.

The two assert.deepEqual calls (now at line 511 and line 555, after the explanatory ISSUE-2ec4d979 comments each cast immediately precedes) have their expected argument cast to the variable's own declared type; ReplyEnvelope and FrameEnvelope are imported as types from channel.ts (line 24). migrationSteps.action: Add a type-only import of ReplyEnvelope and FrameEnvelope from channel.ts to router-session.test.ts.
Cast the expected argument of the assert.deepEqual(replies, [...]) call at line 511 to (ReplyEnvelope | FrameEnvelope)[].
Cast the expected argument of the assert.deepEqual(acks, [], ...) call at line 555 to string[].

migration.backwardCompat: No public or shared API changes; this is a type-only edit confined to one test file. ReplyEnvelope/FrameEnvelope are consumed read-only from their existing export, not modified.

alternativesConsidered.name: Cast the expected argument at each narrowing site
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: At the two assert.deepEqual calls that trigger narrowing, cast the expected literal to the variable's own declared type so the narrowing is a no-op.

alternativesConsidered.name: Switch the two assertions to assert.ok(util.isDeepStrictEqual(...))
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Replace the two narrowing-prone assert.deepEqual calls with assert.ok(isDeepStrictEqual(actual, expected)), which carries no type-narrowing assertion signature.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Also fixes the type error but at a worse debugging/convention cost for no additional benefit over a1 — loses assert.deepEqual's structured diff and introduces a second assertion idiom inconsistent with the rest of the file.

alternativesConsidered.name: Widen the two variables' declared types to prevent useful narrowing
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Declare replies/acks with a type assert.deepEqual cannot narrow usefully, rather than casting at each call site.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Does not actually solve the problem: the narrowing happens at the CALL SITE from expected's inferred type, not from actual's declared type, so no declaration-level type change can prevent it.
